q: With prefix[0] = 0 and prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i], the sum of nums[2..5] is…
why: prefix[6] covers nums[0..5]; subtract prefix[2], which covers nums[0..1].

q: After building prefix sums once, each range sum query costs…
why: It's one subtraction of two stored values.

q: In Subarray Sum Equals K, why start with seen = {0: 1}?
options: So subarrays starting at index 0 are counted
why: A subarray nums[0..i] sums to k when the running sum s equals k, which means s − k = 0 must already be "seen".

q: Why not use a sliding window for Subarray Sum Equals K?
options: With negative numbers, shrinking the window doesn't reliably lower the sum
why: Sliding windows need a monotonic sum: growing only increases it, shrinking only decreases it. Negatives break that.

q: What does this return for nums = [1, 7, 3, 6, 5, 6]?
Product of Array Except Self without division: answer[i] is…
options: product of everything left of i × product of everything right of i
why: Prefix products from the left and suffix products from the right, multiplied together. No division, so zeros are fine.
